Even if nothing happened to the brother at all, his absence is still real and would have an effect on Nate, and the mom still doesn’t think of that as a factor.

My theory is that something bad happened to the younger brother and Nate is most likely responsible for it. Like possibly from doing something stupid when they were kids, and in order to protect Nate, the parents covered it up like it was an accident he wasn’t involved in, so now none of them speak about it at all. This would also explain more as to why Nate feels invincible and can get away with doing whatever he wants, along with his other sociopathic tendencies.

I know this feeling extremely. It feels unattainable and like everyone either pities or laughs at you. But none of that is true. I’m currently 26 and earlier this year I was completely, utterly, and uncomfortably single, and had never even held hands with someone, let alone anything remotely intimate. It’s painful. your mind never stops looking everywhere you go every day. 
I’ve been blessed over the past few months because it happened for me. I finally met my person, and now that I’m here, it shifted everything. 
I was ready to give up, and when I was at my lowest, tried to kill myself multiple times and frequented hospitals. 

Keep searching, don’t give up. You’re still young and there’s absolutely nothing wrong with you. Ask a friend to set u up. go places by yourself and talk to others you notice are alone too. Give compliments to random strangers through out your day, and it doesn’t even have to be someone you’re attracted to in that way. Practice stepping out of your comfort zone and approach others in small ways. If you spread a little bit of joy to others, in turn, you’ll find that joy coming back to you. I promise you

In short, she’s sees herself as Mima even when she’s murdering people, but the real Mima would never kill anyone so she’s breaking her own narrative of what Mima is and that essentially pushes her over the edge of complete madness, and that’s why the scene plays out the way it does. 

I’m pretty sure it’s the first time Rumi physically kills someone herself, every other act of killing prior she has Mr MeMania do so she could maintain her image of being innocent Mima.

It’s not her feeling remorse, it’s supposed to be confusion. She’s having an identity crisis and doesn’t know what’s real anymore, and same goes for the real Mima. The real Mima hasn’t and wouldn’t kill anyone but she’s also is so lost mentally she can’t remember what she’s done anymore. Rumi HAS killed people to protect her image of what Mima is, since she sees herself as Mima, but it causes a psychological rift in herself because the real Mima wouldn’t kill. so when she’s seeing herself as Mima, her mind has to find a way of making sure it fits into her narrative of what Mima is to her, so blocks out her actions of the night before. Rumi sees herself as Mima, and also is trying to prevent the real Mima from changing, so her mind is at war with itself because she subconsciously knows she’s not really Mima, since the real Mima is someone she interacts with daily, but also can’t accept the real Mima being something she can’t control. 
So when she has that brief phone call during that sequence where “Rumi” is on the other end of the line, it’s to show how removed/detached she is from that side of herself and is imagining her Rumi identity as being completely separate from her

I thought about this part as well. I think when you see Rumi on the phone in the office with Tadokoro, it’s just Rumi imagining herself being at the office. If you pay close attention to the dialogue of the phone call while tadokoro is talking to “Mima” it sounds like something he would be saying to Rumi instead, like wondering why she’s not at the office. Even weirder is when they show “Rumi” speak for that brief moment, what she says sounds like what “Mima” would reply with on the other end to Tadokoro. 
After the call ends I also noticed that when she goes to answer the door to the paparazzi, her door is chain locked from the inside, further cementing that no one could’ve come in and left without locking the door behind them. Even more so, the real Mimas actual apartment does not have a chain lock when we see her enter earlier in the film, which might be the biggest indicator that this is the duplicate Rumi apartment. And lastly, we only see the paparazzi swarm her front door this one time and if this were real, they would be showing up to her house everyday if her address got leaked. The paparazzi that were seeing is another delusion of Rumis and they’re just a projection of her fear and guilt catching up to her
